allObjections.title: Phantom atomicity enforcement
allObjections.detail: §7 Output Contract item #5 declares ProductSSOT writes as 'atomic with the rest of the output contract' with mandatory rollback on failure, but P0-5 confirms zero rollback code exists. Every pipeline run today violates this atomicity guarantee silently, creating a false sense of data integrity.

allObjections.title: MessageBus architectural split-brain
allObjections.detail: The real MessageBus.ts has backpressure, TTL, and overflow handling, but api/research-url.js uses a no-op stub that silently drops all 65 canonical topics. This creates two parallel realities where agents think they're communicating but messages vanish into void.

allObjections.title: Dual scoring paths create audit ambiguity
allObjections.detail: ScoreEvaluator.js implements 95/95 threshold per §10 Self-Governance, while AutoRunner uses /50 Monitor scoring. P2-3 confirms the 95/95 path 'isn't shown to the operator' — operators see /50 scores while SSOT declares 95/95 as canonical, creating clearance-gate confusion.

allObjections.title: Agent status taxonomy breakdown
allObjections.detail: Agent #4 is marked SHIPPED-GREEN in §15.1 but P2-10 reveals Stripe Connect isn't wired and deployment shows 'No products registered yet'. The status categories don't distinguish between 'code complete' and 'operationally deployed', making the roster misleading.

allObjections.title: ProductSSOT Unbuilt
allObjections.detail: Section §7.5 describes the ProductSSOT entity as a critical component of the system, yet it is entirely unbuilt. This absence undermines the atomicity of the output contract and the symbiotic feedback loop described in §28, leading to incomplete runs that do not adhere to the SSOT's requirements.

allObjections.title: MessageBus Stub
allObjections.detail: The MessageBus is implemented in src/lib/agents/MessageBus.ts, but api/research-url.js uses a no-op stub. This prevents agents from communicating effectively in production, which is crucial for the integration and operation of multiple agents as described in §15.2.

allObjections.title: GTM Readiness Report Missing
allObjections.detail: Section §7.6 outlines a GTM Readiness Report scoring formula that is not implemented in the codebase. This missing component means that the demo-readiness gate in §11 Clearance Step 5 cannot function as intended, potentially allowing unready products to pass clearance.

allObjections.title: Unbuilt ProductSSOT
allObjections.detail: The ProductSSOT entity is entirely unbuilt, which means that every pipeline run silently bypasses it, making the §7 Output Contract item #5 mandatory and atomic. This is a critical component that is missing, and its absence affects the entire system.

allObjections.title: MessageBus wiring gap
allObjections.detail: The MessageBus is implemented, but it is not wired into the api/research-url.js, which means that agents cannot communicate in production today. This is a significant gap that needs to be addressed.

allObjections.title: Dual QA scoring paths
allObjections.detail: There are two separate code paths for QA scoring, one in ScoreEvaluator.js and another in the AutoRunner /50 Monitor. These paths do not reconcile, and it is unclear which one is canonical. This could lead to inconsistencies and errors in the system.

allObjections.title: Unclear roles in §3
allObjections.detail: The roles and responsibilities within the Commercial Model + Metadata-Driven Architecture section are unclear. The distinction between providers and end-customers, and their respective roles in the metadata-driven architecture, is not well-defined.

allObjections.title: Incomplete Agent #4 status
allObjections.detail: There is a contradiction in the status of Agent #4 Provider Onboarding. The SSOT §15.1 marks it as SHIPPED-GREEN, but the deployment status is listed as DORMANT. This discrepancy needs to be addressed to ensure clarity and consistency.

allObjections.title: MessageBus wiring gap
allObjections.detail: The MessageBus is fully implemented in MessageBus.ts but is used as a no-op stub in api/research-url.js. This means that the 4 ACE topics are never fired, leading to potential communication issues between agents.

allObjections.title: Unclear integration of Agent #4
allObjections.detail: The SSOT §15.1 row 4 states Agent #4 is SHIPPED-GREEN, but the deployment status is DORMANT. This contradiction needs to be addressed. The agent's status should be clearly defined as either PARTIAL or a new status category should be created.

allObjections.title: Incomplete MessageBus wiring
allObjections.detail: The MessageBus is fully implemented in MessageBus.ts but is used as a no-op stub in api/research-url.js. This means that the 4 ACE topics never fire, which is a critical gap. The MessageBus should be properly wired into api/research-url.js to ensure that agents can communicate effectively.

allObjections.title: Dual QA scoring paths
allObjections.detail: There are two separate QA scoring paths: ScoreEvaluator.js uses a 95/95 threshold, while AutoRunner uses a /50 Monitor path. These paths do not reconcile and serve different purposes, which can lead to confusion and inconsistencies in the scoring process.

allObjections.title: ProductSSOT entity unbuilt
allObjections.detail: The ProductSSOT entity is entirely unbuilt, which is a critical gap. The §7 Output Contract item #5 is mandatory and atomic, meaning every pipeline run should write to ProductSSOT. Without this, the integrity of the pipeline runs is compromised.

allObjections.title: Executor Registry complexity
allObjections.detail: The EXECUTOR_REGISTRY (§15.5) adds significant complexity by splitting agent charters and requiring cross-linking between AGENT_REGISTRY and EXECUTOR_REGISTRY. This split charter approach increases cognitive load and potential for inconsistencies.

allObjections.title: Symbiotic Loop cost concerns
allObjections.detail: The Symbiotic Feed-Back Loop (§28) relies on reading and writing the ProductSSOT on every run, which could introduce significant overhead and cost, especially with aggressive crawls and large ProductSSOT sizes. The cost optimization of crawl scope narrowing may not offset the read/write costs.

allObjections.title: Admin override risks
allObjections.detail: Treating admin overrides as CEO-equivalent directives (§28.3) introduces a risk of inconsistent or incorrect behavior if admins make poorly informed decisions. The override mechanism could bypass automated checks and lead to regressions or security vulnerabilities.

allObjections.title: GTM Readiness score gaming
allObjections.detail: The GTM Readiness Report scoring formula (§7.6) is susceptible to gaming.  The fixed weights for severity and visibility could be exploited to artificially inflate the score without addressing underlying issues.

allObjections.title: ProductSSOT unbuilt
allObjections.detail: The audit identifies §7.5 ProductSSOT as entirely unbuilt despite being mandatory for atomic output contracts. No code exists in src/lib/productSSOT or API routes, violating §7 Output Contract item #5. This breaks §28 symbiotic loop pre-run reads and §11 Clearance Step 5 enforcement.

allObjections.title: GTM scoring fiction
allObjections.detail: §7.6 GTM Readiness scoring formula (100 - 10*crit - 5*high etc.) exists only in docs. Production uses legacy /50 Monitor scoring (Defect B fix), making §11 Step 5 prerequisite #2 unenforceable. This creates false demo-readiness signals for products with critical issues.

allObjections.title: MessageBus stubs mislead
allObjections.detail: Agent #21 (Aggressive Crawl) uses no-op MessageBus stubs in api/research-url.js while src/lib/agents/MessageBus.ts implements real pub/sub. This means 4 ENTRY 006 topics (21.crawl.completed.v1 etc.) never fire, breaking CA-9-C customer feedback loops and Agent #26 auto-admission.

allObjections.title: ExecutorRegistry cross-link gap
allObjections.detail: §15.5 Mitigation M1 (AGENT_REGISTRY ↔ EXECUTOR_REGISTRY cross-validation) is unimplemented. validateExecutors() lacks referential checks, risking orphaned executors. This violates CA-7.3 and could cause runtime failures when primary agents reference nonexistent executors.

allObjections.title: No durable bus wiring
allObjections.detail: FA-Q2 and `api/research-url.js` show the handler instantiates an in-memory no-op `messageBus`/`auditLog`, while `MessageBus.ts` itself is explicitly non-durable and single-process only. That means the new Agent #21/ACE topics can appear to exist in code but still vanish at process boundaries, so production observability and inter-agent coordination remain fictional.

allObjections.title: Score paths conflict semantically
allObjections.detail: FA-Q3 exposes two live scoring regimes: `ScoreEvaluator.js` enforces a 95/95 governance/readiness rubric, while the Monitor path still computes a separate /50 aggregate. The proposal says not to reconcile them, but that creates two canonical-looking truths for clearance, which is dangerous because operators will not know which score is authoritative in a blocking decision.

allObjections.title: ProductSSOT atomicity is impossible
allObjections.detail: FA-Q4 and §7.5 require an atomic ProductSSOT write for every output, yet the artifact shows no code surface for ProductSSOT and no write path in the pipeline. Making the run rollback depend on an unimplemented table turns normal renewals into a partial-failure trap: the system can produce a live URL but fail the contractual write and still not have a real rollback mechanism.

allObjections.title: ProductSSOT Unimplemented
allObjections.detail: §7.5 defines ProductSSOT entity, but it's entirely unbuilt (§P0-2). Every pipeline run silently completes without the mandatory atomic write (§7 Output Contract item #5).

allObjections.title: GTM Readiness Report Unbuilt
allObjections.detail: §7.6 defines the canonical demo-readiness scoring formula, but no production code computes it (§P0-3). §11 Clearance Step 5 prerequisite #2 relies on this score.

allObjections.title: Agent #21 MessageBus Topic Emission Unbuilt
allObjections.detail: Agent #21 Aggressive Crawl Conductor charter includes producing `21.crawl.completed.v1`, `21.issues.detected.v1`, `21.gtm.readiness.v1` topics, but `api/research-url.js` uses a no-op stub for MessageBus (§P1-4).

allObjections.title: §7.5 ProductSSOT entity UNBUILT
allObjections.detail: §7 Output Contract item #5 and §7.5 mandate atomic delta_log writes to ProductSSOT on every pipeline run with full rollback on failure; api/renew.js, AutoRunner.jsx and all agents have zero read/write code or tables, so every run silently bypasses the contract.

allObjections.title: Agent #4 status contradiction
allObjections.detail: §15.1 row 4 marks Agent #4 SHIPPED-GREEN (commit 5006431) while §3 explicitly states 'DORMANT today' for Stripe Connect revenue tracking; no deployed webhook or Connect flow exists per audit, violating the commercial model.

allObjections.title: MessageBus no-op stub in production path
allObjections.detail: MessageBus.ts implements real pub/sub with 65 topics and freeze semantics, yet api/research-url.js:30-31 instantiates Agent21 with {publish: async()=>{}, subscribe:()=>{}} so none of 21.crawl.completed.v1, 21.issues.detected.v1 or 21.gtm.readiness.v1 ever fire.

strongest_rejection_argument.text: The strongest case for rejecting or deferring is that the proposal mixes three independent canonicalization efforts—Agent #21 wiring, scoring authority, and ProductSSOT persistence—without first resolving the foundational storage and contract layer. If ProductSSOT is absent and the bus is a stub, then formalizing new clearance behavior risks freezing a misleading architecture in place and increasing operational complexity before the system can actually honor its own atomicity and audit promises. Deferral would let the team implement the storage and event backbone first, then reconcile the divergent scoring paths with real telemetry.

FA-Q2.rationale: The MessageBus is the core communication mechanism. Without it, the agents are effectively isolated, negating the benefits of the agent-based architecture.

FA-Q3.pick_text: REJECT — requires architectural redesign before either can be canonical; surface the misalignment to CEO before any fix.
FA-Q3.rationale: Having two separate scoring paths creates confusion and undermines the integrity of the QA process. A clear, unified approach is needed.

FA-Q4.pick_text: P0 — build ProductSSOT before any agent wave begins (agents write to it; without it, §7 atomicity is fiction).
FA-Q4.rationale: The ProductSSOT is fundamental to the symbiotic loop and the atomicity guarantees. It should be built before relying on agents to write to it.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal attempts to address several gaps but introduces significant complexity and leaves key components unbuilt. A more incremental and focused approach may be more effective.

objections.title: ProductSSOT unbuilt
objections.detail: The audit identifies §7.5 ProductSSOT as entirely unbuilt despite being mandatory for atomic output contracts. No code exists in src/lib/productSSOT or API routes, violating §7 Output Contract item #5. This breaks §28 symbiotic loop pre-run reads and §11 Clearance Step 5 enforcement.

objections.title: GTM scoring fiction
objections.detail: §7.6 GTM Readiness scoring formula (100 - 10*crit - 5*high etc.) exists only in docs. Production uses legacy /50 Monitor scoring (Defect B fix), making §11 Step 5 prerequisite #2 unenforceable. This creates false demo-readiness signals for products with critical issues.

objections.title: MessageBus stubs mislead
objections.detail: Agent #21 (Aggressive Crawl) uses no-op MessageBus stubs in api/research-url.js while src/lib/agents/MessageBus.ts implements real pub/sub. This means 4 ENTRY 006 topics (21.crawl.completed.v1 etc.) never fire, breaking CA-9-C customer feedback loops and Agent #26 auto-admission.

objections.title: ExecutorRegistry cross-link gap
objections.detail: §15.5 Mitigation M1 (AGENT_REGISTRY ↔ EXECUTOR_REGISTRY cross-validation) is unimplemented. validateExecutors() lacks referential checks, risking orphaned executors. This violates CA-7.3 and could cause runtime failures when primary agents reference nonexistent executors.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If implemented without fixing P0-3, products with critical XSS issues could achieve 'Showcase-ready' scores because the legacy /50 scoring inflates results, whereas the status quo at least surfaces raw vulnerability counts. This could lead to demoing compromised products to prospects, causing reputational damage.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: This proposal should be rejected because it documents gaps without providing remediation timelines or resource allocation. The 25 unresolved items (including 5 P0 blockers) reveal systemic architectural debt that cannot be patched incrementally. Deferring to a comprehensive rebuild of the agent-orchestration substrate would be safer than attempting to fix these interconnected gaps piecemeal.

FA-Q1.pick_text: Reclassify Agent #4 as PARTIAL — code exists but deployment is incomplete; SSOT §15.1 status row updated.
FA-Q1.rationale: The SHIPPED-GREEN label misrepresents reality; PARTIAL accurately reflects coded-but-not-deployed state while preserving the charter's validity.

FA-Q2.pick_text: Wire MessageBus into api/research-url.js as P0 — no-op stub means agents cannot communicate in production today.
FA-Q2.rationale: The stub creates illusion of functionality; real MessageBus is implemented and must be connected to enable Agent #10/#26 message flows.

FA-Q3.pick_text: Keep both — they serve different purposes (95/95 = governance audit gate; /50 = demo readiness score).
FA-Q3.rationale: ScoreEvaluator's 95/95 governs agent clearance while /50 measures product demo health; reconciling them prematurely would conflate distinct concerns.

FA-Q4.pick_text: P0 — build ProductSSOT before any agent wave begins (agents write to it; without it, §7 atomicity is fiction).
FA-Q4.rationale: ProductSSOT is foundational to §7 output contracts and §28 symbiotic loops; deferring it would cascade inaccuracies through all agent operations.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The audit excellently exposes 'sounds-done-isn't' gaps but lacks severity-weighted sequencing. P0-2 (ProductSSOT) and P0-4 (Agent #21 wiring) should precede P0-1 (auth traversal) to avoid building on unstable substrate.

objections.title: No durable bus wiring
objections.detail: FA-Q2 and `api/research-url.js` show the handler instantiates an in-memory no-op `messageBus`/`auditLog`, while `MessageBus.ts` itself is explicitly non-durable and single-process only. That means the new Agent #21/ACE topics can appear to exist in code but still vanish at process boundaries, so production observability and inter-agent coordination remain fictional.

objections.title: Score paths conflict semantically
objections.detail: FA-Q3 exposes two live scoring regimes: `ScoreEvaluator.js` enforces a 95/95 governance/readiness rubric, while the Monitor path still computes a separate /50 aggregate. The proposal says not to reconcile them, but that creates two canonical-looking truths for clearance, which is dangerous because operators will not know which score is authoritative in a blocking decision.

objections.title: ProductSSOT atomicity is impossible
objections.detail: FA-Q4 and §7.5 require an atomic ProductSSOT write for every output, yet the artifact shows no code surface for ProductSSOT and no write path in the pipeline. Making the run rollback depend on an unimplemented table turns normal renewals into a partial-failure trap: the system can produce a live URL but fail the contractual write and still not have a real rollback mechanism.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If Agent #21 starts emitting crawl findings into a no-op bus while clearance continues to read the /50 Monitor path, operators can get a green-ish demo score without the critical issues ever reaching downstream consumers. That is worse than the status quo because it gives a false sense of integration and may let broken products pass review with no auditable signal trail.
adversarial.precedent: The React `setState` race / lost update class of bugs is a real-world analogue: in-memory, non-atomic coordination produced states that looked valid locally but were inconsistent across observers. More directly, many message-queue systems have suffered from "appears published but never consumed" failures when teams treated ephemeral or stubbed buses as production plumbing.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The strongest case for rejecting or deferring is that the proposal mixes three independent canonicalization efforts—Agent #21 wiring, scoring authority, and ProductSSOT persistence—without first resolving the foundational storage and contract layer. If ProductSSOT is absent and the bus is a stub, then formalizing new clearance behavior risks freezing a misleading architecture in place and increasing operational complexity before the system can actually honor its own atomicity and audit promises. Deferral would let the team implement the storage and event backbone first, then reconcile the divergent scoring paths with real telemetry.

FA-Q1.pick_text: Reclassify Agent #4 as PARTIAL — code exists but deployment is incomplete; SSOT §15.1 status row updated.
FA-Q1.rationale: The artifact itself describes a contradiction between SSOT and deployment reality, so a split between shipped code and incomplete rollout is the most precise status. This preserves the distinction between implementation existence and operational readiness.

FA-Q2.pick_text: Wire MessageBus into api/research-url.js as P0 — no-op stub means agents cannot communicate in production today.
FA-Q2.rationale: The handler currently injects a stub, so the new topics are effectively dead even though the bus implementation exists. Given Agent #21 and clearance dependencies, wiring the real bus is a blocking foundation task, not a later optimization.

FA-Q3.pick_text: REJECT — requires architectural redesign before either can be canonical; surface the misalignment to CEO before any fix.
FA-Q3.rationale: The two scores serve different control planes and the artifact explicitly refuses to reconcile them. Until one authority model is chosen, picking either score as canonical would institutionalize ambiguity in clearance gating.

FA-Q4.pick_text: P0 — build ProductSSOT before any agent wave begins (agents write to it; without it, §7 atomicity is fiction).
FA-Q4.rationale: The SSOT makes ProductSSOT mandatory and atomic, and multiple sections depend on it for read-before-run and write-after-run behavior. If it doesn't exist, the contract cannot be satisfied and every downstream agent-wave feature is built on an unenforceable premise.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal reads like a diagnostic inventory, but it also implicitly legitimizes several incomplete seams as if they were operational. The biggest risk is not any single missing feature; it's that multiple partially-wired subsystems together create a convincing but false narrative of end-to-end control.
